cands: Affirmative conclusion from a negative premise
Confusing an explanation with an excuse

items.text: If they had just talked to each other instead of ending it over text, they’d definitely be married by now.

The HR rep in our building keeps saying that dating coworkers is always a disaster, so I’m going to avoid it. She handles payroll, and if she’s seen enough office drama to say that, she probably knows what she’s talking about.
Our clinic's diabetic patients as a group tend to have high blood pressure, so if Eric has diabetes, he probably has high blood pressure too.
The lab coin has come up tails seven flips straight, so I'm certain the next run will be heads. Random is random, but it can't keep mocking us like this.
"That training load is why our striker isn’t recovering well." If I have to read that twice to follow it, then it sounds like a made-up excuse to me.
The budget numbers don't add up for another raise right now, but I'm not worried. If you have the right kind of faith in the company, you'll see this bonus is coming.
After seeing a few plastic bags snagged in the river near my neighborhood, it’s obvious our city has no real environmental plan. If that’s what the cleanup looks like, the whole program is a joke.
If you still think that last call was bad, you’re ignoring the xG, PPDA, VAR, G+A, and B2B numbers, so I’m not going to take your take seriously.

Ms. Darrow keeps saying chemistry labs are like recipes because the steps have to be followed in order. Recipes are basically the same kind of thing as restaurant operating manuals: they tell people how to produce the same result every time. So her class should be run like a restaurant kitchen, with students judged on speed, uniformity, and how closely they obey instructions rather than on whether they understand the chemistry.
The dictionary defines a tablet as a small flat device, so it doesn't make sense to call this foldable laptop a tablet at all. If the shape isn't exactly listed, the label is wrong.
If the IT lead is pushing this laptop brand, I’m not taking it seriously; his department’s budget is already tied to the vendor’s discounts.

A: He said he needed space, but that usually means he’s realizing the relationship matters and he’s just sorting out his feelings. B: So you think the silence is actually a good sign? A: Exactly, because people pull away when they’re trying not to rush back too soon.
People are saying homework is stressing everyone out, but the best way to fix that is to assign more homework so students can get over the stress from homework faster.
Did your manager ever explain why your team gets rewarded for missing deadlines?
I looked at the app reviews, and five-star ratings are clustered around phones launched in spring. That’s enough for me to say spring releases are just better tech.
If one pastor says the prayer group helps and another says it's just a habit, then what are we supposed to believe? People who study religion clearly don't know enough for any real answer.

“We shouldn’t tell visitors the relic has healing power when there’s no good evidence it has ever healed anyone.” “Unless you can prove there is no healing power in it at all, you have no grounds for doubting what the church says about it.”
That team is clearly the best in the league because they win so much, and they win so much because they’re the best in the league.
I asked three times whether your dog bit the neighbor’s kid, and you just stared at the floor. That tells me your dog did it.
Stop acting like the bank fees are normal; the app showing my balance dropping every week is all the proof you need that they’re draining us on purpose.
A: Every runner on the relay team is a varsity athlete. B: And every varsity athlete is cleared for the 5K trial. So some runners on the relay team are definitely cleared for the 5K trial.

If the new raid strategy is so good, why does it still feel wrong when I watch it? We should stick with the old one, because my instincts say the new setup isn't the way this game is meant to be played.
"A higher sensitivity is always better in shooters." That's just common sense if you've played anything competitive. If your aim is good, the faster setting clearly makes you better.
We need the new surveillance bill because if we don't pass it, the city will be helpless the next time something goes wrong on the subway, and nobody wants to be the one blamed when panic breaks out.

A: “The clinic says my headaches are probably from stress.” B: They say that because they know your blood pressure spikes every night after you lie awake checking your phone, and the nurse who called you back has already marked it as a pattern.
"It was just a dumb comedy show." No, it was cruel, and if you didn’t feel how insulting that scene was, you’re ignoring what was right in front of you.

I know Cara says daycare helps kids learn to share, but she’s paying for the fancy private center downtown, so I’m not buying her take. If she were right, she wouldn’t need to spend that much to prove it.

Our manager’s new check-in routine has people hitting deadlines more consistently, so I’m convinced it’s the right way to measure productivity. If a method gets better results, that’s evidence the method reflects the truth.
You keep saying science changes its mind, but that’s exactly why we should treat every established rule as fixed once it’s taught. If it’s in a textbook, it must hold in every case.
"Maybe the quiz was just a bad day," but that means the grade could be inflated, so I shouldn't trust it for the final average.

You can keep saying the results are consistent with the normal error rate, but this sample is different because the lab tech looked nervous and the equipment was new. That’s why I’m sure the finding is real and not just one of those typical false alarms.
You said the concert is either worth the ticket price or it isn't. Honestly, I think it's more about who went with us and what mood you were in, so the price question doesn't really decide anything.
Look, everybody who actually shops after work knows the family pack is the smart buy. If you’re a normal person trying to stretch a grocery budget, you don’t need to overthink it.

You can pray all you want, and if nothing changes, that only shows the faith is being tested; if things do change, then the answer came through the prayer. Either way, the temple signs and the quiet in my chest tell me I’m on the right path.

A: We really should compare neighborhood crime stats before we sign this lease.
B: Forget that—our realtor said the building is one of the safest in town, and she sells houses all day. If she thinks it’s fine, that’s probably the truth.

All students who submit homework on time are students who receive credit for it. All students who receive credit for homework are treated by the school as responsible. Therefore, no students who submit homework on time are treated by the school as responsible.
I watched one documentary about electric cars and the battery was dead in a year, so these things are clearly unreliable. I’m not trusting a whole industry based on that mess.

The reason that promotion fell through was that the manager had already decided, at 2:14 p.m. on Tuesday, to give it to someone from accounting, and he only kept talking to you in the hallway because he didn’t want the team to hear the real plan.

The article says the classroom ventilation study tracked infection rates for a year, compared similar schools, and included attendance records, but the photo of the researchers tells me enough. They are standing there in pristine white coats in front of a shiny new air unit, so this is mostly about making the project look impressive. I don’t see why everyone is focusing on their charts when the presentation is so obviously staged.

"The new lab result is probably the one where the reaction sped up, the catalyst stayed stable, and the sample stayed pure." That seems more likely than just the reaction speeding up, because all three happening together points to the right mechanism.

A: What do you mean by "being saved"?
B: It's when your soul gets aligned with the higher order in a way that keeps it from collapsing into separation.
A: That still doesn't tell me how to actually become saved.
School is already set up to sort kids by test scores and deadlines, so that must be the right way to do it.
“You said the pastor's plan for the food drive is solid.” I don't care if the numbers add up; that church has been smug about every neighborhood issue, so I'm not giving their project a pass.
If the mosque is really about peace, why does it make so many people feel guilty for missing one service?

I keep seeing streamers say they got good at this shooter by “just grinding ranked,” and they’re the ones still playing after years, so that’s clearly the way to improve. If that method worked badly, those people would’ve quit long ago.
I’ve sunk 120 hours into this save file and I’m this close to beating the boss, so there’s no way I’m deleting it now and starting over.
The market panic is overblown when you understand the EBITDA, ROI, P/E, EPS, and CFO guidance behind the quarter. That’s why the stock is still a buy.
“I light candles when I pray, and the prayers help me feel calmer; the rituals also connect me to my family’s faith.” “So you admit it’s just about feeling calm.”

I just sat through another meeting where people kept talking about blessings and purpose like it was obvious. Honestly, the whole place feels spiritually empty to me, so this company clearly has no real faith in anything. Please stop pretending it does.

If management lets one dog stay at a desk for an hour, people will start bringing in bigger pets, then someone’s going to be walking a cat around the office, and after that the place turns into a daycare for animals.
We need a city rule that limits rent hikes; don’t tell me that means “every landlord” because technically some leases are corporate, not personal, so the proposal is already careless.

If you're asking me, the reason that toddler is still melting down at bedtime is that his dad is a selfish disaster who can't organize a grocery list, so of course his parenting takes the easy way out.

I know that documentary was well reviewed, but if one scene offends the wrong sponsor, the whole series could get pulled from streaming and everyone’s subscription money is wasted. Better not bother with it.
I’m more likely to find a shiny in this one run than to get a shiny or a rare drop. The drop table is huge, and that combined outcome feels way too broad to hit tonight.
A: "This restaurant has amazing reviews." B: Maybe, but food ought to be healthy if it’s any good, and this menu has too much fried stuff for that to be true.

This office app is like a treadmill because it keeps people moving, and treadmills are like physical therapy because both are used for recovery. So after switching to this app, our team should see it as a medical tool.

Our manager says we need to keep every scene schedule on track, but the new streaming show ran overtime every week and people loved it. If they can ignore the clock and still get good reviews, why are we acting like our video has to be so rigid?

A: My doctor says my headaches are probably from stress.
B: A naturopath on a wellness site said every headache like that means your liver is overloaded, so I’m following that instead.

If the poll numbers look bad for that candidate, it's probably because the survey missed the right voters. We shouldn't treat the results as meaningful until the missing data show up and fix the picture.

"That lab only tested a dozen different markers, so I wouldn't read too much into the one that lit up." That's exactly the point: with that many markers, the one strong result is the one that matters, so the supplement probably really does improve recovery.

You’re saying the meeting ended before we assigned volunteers and now the Saturday table may be uncovered. I understand that’s frustrating, but the meeting is over, and I don’t see any value in revisiting how it ended.
Keeping the coach and the captain together is what makes a team work. Split that up and you lose the whole identity of the squad.
The ticket was unfair because I clearly broke the rule by mistake, but also there was never any rule to begin with, so they had no business writing me up.
The managers keep debating whether remote Fridays improved output, but if they can't agree, then nobody knows whether the policy worked and we should stop pretending there’s an answer.
I know the report is late, but I’ve been covering for two people since Monday and barely slept, so cutting my bonus over this would be harsh. The delay should be overlooked.
I know you say the kid’s behavior is a phase, but I’m too angry to buy that. If it makes the staff this frustrated, there has to be something seriously wrong at home.
The river flooded because people left a few plastic bottles near the bank. If those bottles hadn’t been there, this wouldn’t have happened.

I know he forgot our anniversary because work has been brutal and he's been sleeping four hours a night, so I shouldn't be upset about it. The whole thing makes sense once you know how exhausted he is.
gold: Confusing an explanation with an excuse

items.text: "He stays up late because of school or because he’s on his phone." If he’s on his phone, then it’s not school making him tired, so I’m taking the charger tonight.
In competitive gaming, the best teams win because they practice harder than everyone else, and they also win mainly because skill doesn’t matter much.
That airport was built in the wrong place, plain and simple; if the city council had seen the flood data we have now, they never would have approved it.
The app says the password must be eight characters, but that sounds like a sign to keep my account spiritually open, not a real rule. Tech messages sometimes speak in a deeper way.
"If a neighborhood really values clean air, it will support fewer diesel trucks." This neighborhood supports fewer diesel trucks, so it must really value clean air.

I prayed every night this month and finally got that interview, so I know the church has been answering me. I’m not mentioning the weeks I prayed just as hard and nothing happened, because the timing of this one blessing says enough.

A: “Our school should stop ranking students by who can memorize fastest.” B: “But that’s how schools usually do it, and it’s been that way for years. If a method is the standard in most classrooms, it’s probably the right way to measure learning.”
People who live near the river keep saying the new factory will hurt water quality, but they’re obviously just worried about property values, so this alarmism isn’t worth sharing.

The director’s cut didn’t ruin the movie. Those scenes were never removed in the first place, and if they were removed, they were useless filler, and besides, taking them out is what preserved the emotional arc everyone is praising.

A: Did you hear about that manager who took credit for his team’s work? B: That’s exactly what office culture is now—people stepping on each other and stealing ideas. Once you’ve seen one boss do it, you know that’s how workplaces run.
That reboot was not a clever twist; it was a lazy, cash-grab sequel dressed up with nostalgia. If a studio has to milk fans like that, the movie is obviously awful.

Everyone on this team is using less paper and switching off their monitors at night, so this office is definitely environmentally responsible. When every person does their bit, the whole place is green.
Nessa spent months writing long messages, buying little gifts, and planning every detail, so her partner must really be the one for her.
I know the city’s new bike lanes cut traffic; sure, there are a few intersections where cars still back up, but that just means they reduce traffic in the places that matter.

A: We should get the algebra tutor; half the class failed the last quiz.
B: No, we’re not hiring a tutor. I’ve made the decision, and that’s all the reason you need.

When you say, “The daycare sends too much homework and ignores parents,” it sounds like you’re really more aligned with those no-structure co-op families than with this daycare community. If our approach bothers you that much, you should stop dragging everyone down and enroll somewhere that shares your values.
If we had adopted that rescue dog earlier, she would already be house-trained and sleeping through the night by now.
"The new telescope theory sounds elegant and beautifully simple." Exactly—that clean, elegant wording is why it has to be the right explanation for the signal.
If economists can't even agree on whether the rent cap helps, then no one really knows anything about it, and the whole debate is just noise.
If the school is serious about later start times, then I suppose we should also install nap pods in every hallway and call algebra optional. That idea is just not realistic.

Maybe the city doesn’t want to hear it, but the recycling push is getting mocked for the same reason solar panels were mocked years ago. When a change threatens the usual habits, people always call it unrealistic first. That’s why I think the plan is probably on the right track.
If the apartment had serious mold, the walls would smell damp and the paint would peel. The walls smell damp and the paint is peeling, so this place definitely has serious mold.
Just checked the dictionary: a coach is someone who trains a team, so our captain can't be a real coach if he mostly handles lineups and motivation. The word doesn't cover that stuff.

Everyone in office keeps acting like the new plan is normal, but people are scared and angry for a reason: it’s another step toward a cold, soulless government that treats ordinary people like numbers. If you care about decency, you know this has to be stopped.

B: The clinic’s exercise plan and lower-sodium meals already help. A: Not really—unless the treatment can guarantee nobody ever gets another symptom and every lab result stays perfect, it’s basically useless.
No, I’m not installing that update. Tech bloggers say once your phone starts pushing these updates, it slows down within a week, so I’m keeping mine as is.
Don’t book that hostel just because the map app recommends it; the app got the listing from the hostel’s own ad, so it’s obviously not a real option.
If my phone battery can last all day on one charge, then this new laptop should too. They both have screens and a power button, so the laptop should be just as efficient.
“All compatible partners are emotionally available, and all people in that dating pool are compatible partners, so some people in that dating pool are emotionally available.”
If a billionaire investor says the budget cuts are necessary, they’re probably right; you don’t build that kind of fortune by misunderstanding numbers.

I get that the patch made the raid bosses spike harder, but people keep ignoring how the new skin bundle actually fixes the game's look. The menu art feels cleaner now, and that's what really matters to most players.
Our forward gets a red card for a hard tackle, so the other team should get one too on their next foul. Equal teams, equal calls. Otherwise the league is treating one side differently for no reason.
I get that the old museum had flaws, but if we can’t rebuild the whole place exactly as it was and recover every detail of city life from that era, then the restoration project feels pointless.
I found the exact bill I was missing in the jacket pocket right after the bank called about the overdraft, so maybe it was just bad luck. Nothing to do with me keeping track poorly, I guess.
A lot of engineers use this cloud tool, and that’s enough for me to trust it. If most people in the field rely on it, then it’s the best option.

B: “Some shows on that app are worth watching.”
A: Then some shows that aren’t worth watching aren’t on that app.

"This meal plan is unhealthy?" I’ve been eating the same salad and grilled chicken for two weeks and I’ve lost eight pounds, so it’s clearly working. The doctor doesn’t need to see the snacks, late-night takeout, or the headaches if the scale is moving down.

When judges start giving people ankle monitors for shoplifting, I think the system has gone too far; I read about one teenager who was shackled for stealing baby formula. That kind of case shows the law is broken.
“He’ll finish the report or at least send the draft tonight” is less believable than “he’ll send the draft tonight,” because the full claim asks for too much.
This movie review says streaming services should stop raising prices, yet the writer clearly pays for three different subscriptions. That makes the whole complaint hard to take seriously.

B: “My doctor says I should cut back on caffeine.” A: Then the rest of us should finally get serious about banning energy drinks at work. Once someone mentions health, it’s usually because it’s time to make the policy change I’ve been pushing.
My cat has every right to nap on the couch, so I should let her stay there even when it’s covered in fresh laundry and I need the space.
“My cat knows when I’m upset because there’s a little watcher in her head checking my face and telling her what mood I’m in.”

The guy in the next cubicle kept borrowing my charger without asking, so I started taking office supplies from his desk when he’s away. He used my things first, so I don’t see why I should be the only one being polite.

“If the manager can show the Friday shift is covered, I’ll stop objecting to the schedule change.”
“She sent the updated roster—Friday has two people on closing.”
“That only proves Friday. I still don’t see written confirmation for Saturday.”
“She added Saturday too, and payroll approved the extra hours.”
“Fine, but until she also gets each employee to sign that they personally like the new hours, I’m not accepting that this schedule problem is resolved.”
If you think this tax plan helps working people, you’re not looking at the numbers. It’s obvious that giving the government more money means less freedom for everyone.

A: "The new app is better because usage is up 18% and crash reports are down." B: Then it must be better, because the only things that matter are the stats. If people say the interface feels clunky or the search is confusing, that’s just subjective noise.
You can say that empire was brutal, but look at the roads, the aqueducts, and the literature it left behind. That tells you the whole system was a success.
This pasta is the best thing on the menu—well, the best if you count only the days when the kitchen isn’t slammed and they don’t overcook it. Which is exactly what I meant.
“The river is still dirty.” I don’t think so; I really want the cleanup to have worked, and the city finally acted, so the water is probably safe now.

That new lab report says the satellite might be safe to launch, but I wouldn’t trust it. If the software misses one tiny error, the whole mission could blow up, so we should delay it until every possible issue is gone.
By 'budget room,' I mean the zone where money has already been translated into available liquidity after fixed obligations have finished compressing it.
A good team always keeps its starters in until the end, so pulling the goalie late is just bad coaching. If you trust your players, you leave the lineup alone no matter what the score is.
The empire either collapsed because of economic strain or because of the border wars. It clearly was the border wars, so the economic strain wasn’t the real cause.

A: "That training app helped my speed a lot." B: "Maybe, but a runner should stick to natural conditioning. If the body is built to improve through miles and drills, all that tech-heavy coaching is just getting in the way."

The council should not vote on park funding by itself. Parks, riverfront apartment limits, and open-space zoning are one package; separating them would gut the whole neighborhood plan and leave us with neither livable housing nor protected green space. If members really care about parks, they need to pass the apartment restrictions at the same time.
"Your itinerary says we leave at 9:00, but the train actually departs at 9:07, so your whole plan is wrong."

I went back through last year’s brokerage chat and there were buys scattered across the whole calendar, but the accounts I circled from January 9 to 12 are all up now. That four-day stretch is the real signal, so the smart move is to buy during the next mid-January dip instead of sitting on cash for rent worries.
A: "You shouldn't have left the puppy alone all day." B: He was barking nonstop, and I had already been up since 5 trying to calm him down, so I needed a break. That's why leaving him was fine.
gold: Confusing an explanation with an excuse

items.text: "Rent went up because the building needed repairs." That may explain this year’s increase, but I’ll only accept it if they also prove the repairs were necessary, the contractor was local, the landlord didn’t make a profit, and the whole complex will be cheaper next year.

I know the test showed the treatment plan needs to change, but after all the panic attacks I’ve had this month, I can’t handle another medication switch right now. Please just keep me on the same prescription.

If you’re deciding whether to get the flu shot, remember that particles can be in two states at once until they’re measured, so the body can handle illness in more than one way. That means the vaccine is basically unnecessary for healthy adults.
No player who ignores the coach's plan will be a steady starter. Some players on this roster ignore the coach's plan. So some players on this roster will be steady starters.
gold: Affirmative conclusion from a negative premise

items.text: "All test tubes are lab equipment." No garden hoses are test tubes. So no garden hoses are lab equipment.
Put the cat door in the laundry room; because I said that’s where it belongs, that’s where it goes.

It sounds like you want a simple date for when the rail line opened, but that's not really how history works. A proper date is just the official moment when the event becomes historically legible through the archive of what was already happening.

My lease allows pets, and there’s no rule saying I have to keep my cat in a carrier when maintenance comes by. Since I’m allowed to let her roam the apartment, that’s what I should do instead of shutting her in the bedroom just because the repair crew prefers it.
